title: Lawmakers Questioned the Clintons About Epstein, Pizzagate and UFOs
description_medium: An Associated Press report published March 2, 2026, described House Oversight Committee videos of Bill and Hillary Clinton’s closed-door depositions. The committee had spent months seeking their testimony. Hillary Clinton said she did not recall meeting Jeffrey Epstein and had no knowledge of his crimes; she also said members asked about UFOs and the debunked Pizzagate conspiracy. Her deposition was briefly paused after Rep. Lauren Boebert sent an unauthorized photograph from the room to a conservative influencer.
description_long: The House Oversight Committee released videos on March 2, 2026, of depositions it had held the previous week with Bill and Hillary Clinton as part of its Jeffrey Epstein investigation. The Associated Press reported that the committee had spent six months trying to question them. Hillary Clinton said she had no knowledge of Epstein’s or Ghislaine Maxwell’s crimes and did not recall meeting Epstein. She also said lawmakers asked her about UFOs and Pizzagate, a false conspiracy theory. Her deposition briefly stopped after Rep. Lauren Boebert sent a photograph from inside the session to an online influencer, violating committee rules. Bill Clinton’s testimony focused on his past relationship with Epstein; he said he saw no signs of abuse and had done nothing wrong. The AP account said Republicans appeared ready to turn to other witnesses after the depositions. These details show a hearing process that included substantive questions, procedural controversy and fringe topics. They do not by themselves show what evidence the committee obtained or establish a broader political motive.

rationale: The hearing account supports the subjects raised and the deposition interruption; it does not establish that the proceeding was merely theatrical or what new evidence resulted.

title: Minnesota Prosecutor Opened an Inquiry Into 17 Incidents Involving Federal Immigration Agents
description_medium: On March 2, 2026, Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty said her office was investigating 17 incidents involving possible unlawful conduct by federal immigration agents during Operation Metro Surge. The Associated Press and Minnesota reporting identified two examples: Border Patrol official Greg Bovino’s use of a chemical irritant near Mueller Park on Jan. 21, and federal agents’ actions at Roosevelt High School on Jan. 7. Moriarty asked the public to submit photos, videos and eyewitness accounts through a new county portal.
description_long: Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced on March 2, 2026, that her office was examining 17 incidents of possible unlawful conduct by federal immigration agents during Operation Metro Surge. The Associated Press reported that one case involved Border Patrol official Greg Bovino throwing a smoke canister toward protesters near Mueller Park on Jan. 21. Another involved federal agents using chemical irritants while making an arrest outside Roosevelt High School on Jan. 7, with students and staff nearby. Moriarty launched a public portal for photos, video and eyewitness accounts and said prosecutors would pursue charges where appropriate. She described the legal question of prosecuting federal agents under state law as difficult and said the federal government had not provided information to her office. The Department of Homeland Security argued that federal officers acting within their duties were immune from state liability. These are competing positions in an open investigation, not a court ruling. Moriarty’s announcement identified possible incidents under review; it did not establish that any officer committed a crime or predict which cases would result in charges.
rationale: The dated announcement, 17 incidents, two named examples and opposing statements on immunity make the inquiry’s scope clear while preserving its preliminary status.

title: Bill Clinton Told Congress He Saw No Signs of Epstein’s Abuse and Had Done Nothing Wrong
description_medium: Former President Bill Clinton testified to the House Oversight Committee on Feb. 27, 2026, about his past relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. The Associated Press reported that the closed-door deposition lasted more than six hours and that lawmakers said he answered every question. In his opening statement, Clinton said he had done nothing wrong and saw no signs of Epstein’s sexual abuse. He said he had stopped associating with Epstein before Epstein’s 2008 guilty plea.
description_long: Bill Clinton appeared before the House Oversight Committee in Chappaqua, New York, on Feb. 27, 2026, for a closed-door deposition about his connection to Jeffrey Epstein. The Associated Press reported that the questioning lasted more than six hours and that lawmakers said Clinton answered every question. In his opening statement, Clinton said he saw no signs of Epstein’s abuse and had done nothing wrong. He said he had stopped associating with Epstein before Epstein’s 2008 guilty plea. Committee chair James Comer said Republicans wanted to know why Clinton maintained a relationship with Epstein after the financier had been convicted in Florida. Democrats renewed calls for President Donald Trump to testify, with one member saying lawmakers were questioning the wrong president. The deposition marked the first time a former U.S. president had been compelled to testify to Congress. AP reported that Clinton was not accused of wrongdoing and that the committee planned to review the testimony. These details establish the stated scope and responses, not a finding about the underlying relationship.

title: NPR Found Missing Epstein-File Pages Related to Allegations Involving Trump
description_medium: An NPR investigation published Feb. 24, 2026, compared Justice Department records with FBI case files and discovery logs and found dozens of pages catalogued by the department but absent from its public Epstein-files database. NPR reported that the missing material included more than 50 pages of interview records and notes concerning a woman who alleged that Jeffrey Epstein introduced her to Donald Trump when she was a minor. The allegation is unverified; NPR reported that agents marked most allegations in related FBI lists as unverifiable or not credible.
description_long: NPR reported on Feb. 24, 2026, that its review of serial numbers, FBI case records, emails and discovery logs identified dozens of Epstein-related pages catalogued by the Justice Department but not visible in the public database. More than 50 pages appeared to concern interviews and notes related to an allegation that Epstein introduced a woman to Donald Trump when she was a minor. NPR said the allegation appeared in FBI summaries, while agents had marked most claims in related lists as unverifiable or not credible. Only one of four FBI interviews with that woman was available in the database, and NPR also found records related to a separate witness that had been temporarily removed and partly restored. The Justice Department said files may be taken down for additional review when victims or their counsel raise concerns, and cited the need for further redactions. The report concerns the completeness and changing contents of a public records release. It does not verify the underlying allegations or establish that political sensitivity caused the omissions.
